item.title: How Arizona State football can still make Big 12 championship game
item.description: A post from the Big 12 Conference on X recently caught our eye for pointing out that the Arizona State football team was one of seven teams in the conference still in contention for the Big 12 championship game. Yes, the ASU football team has not been eliminated from the Big 12 title chase yet, joining Utah, Texas Tech, BYU, Arizona , Houston and Baylor. We couldn't believe it. The Sun Devils are currently tied with Houston, Baylor and Arizona for third in the conference at 4-3, trailing Utah (7-0), Texas Tech (6-1) and BYU (5-2). The top two teams in the conference make the Big 12 championship game, which is scheduled for Friday, Dec. 4, 2026, at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas, and Arizona State has a path to be one of those teams (albeit an extremely narrow path). Who wins? Arizona State vs Oklahoma State picks, predictions, odds for Big 12 game The chase continues 🏆 🏈 Tiebreaker central https://t.co/LKe2lRbODz 🎟️ Secure your tickets now https://t.co/Tcwi8wnfrv pic.twitter.com/HQe89xvGo0 — Big 12 Conference (@Big12Conference) November 17, 2026 How Arizona State can make the 2026 Big 12 championship game So what is Arizona State's path to the Big 12 title game? In Week 12 this week , the Sun Devils need to beat Oklahoma State and have UCF beat Iowa State, Baylor beat Texas Tech, Colorado beat Cincinnati, Kansas beat BYU, Kansas State beat Arizona, West Virginia beat Houston and Utah beat TCU. Then in Week 13, Arizona State needs to beat Arizona and have TCU beat Texas Tech, West Virginia beat Utah, BYU beat Cincinnati, Baylor beat Houston, Colorado beat UCF, Kansas State beat Iowa State and Oklahoma State beat Kansas. If every single one of those results were to happen, Arizona State would win a 4-way tiebreaker based on conference opponent win percentage to join Utah in the Big 12 championship game. That is one monstrous if . Every one of those results falling Arizona State's way would be nearly impossible odds at best, but ASU being even anywhere near contention for the Big 12 title this season seems like a huge win for the program after the Sun Devils fell to 4-4 overall and 2-3 in the Big 12 with the loss to BYU on Oct. 31. So you're telling me there's a chance, huh? item.title: Will the top Penn State football running back play vs Rutgers?
item.description: It's uncertain whether one of the top-trending running backs in the Big Ten will be able to play for Penn State football on Senior Day. Carson Hansen , one of those Nittany Lion seniors, is in "questionable" status for the Saturday, Nov. 21 game against Rutgers in Beaver Stadium, according to coach Matt Campbell . Hansen was in the midst of a career-game performance last Saturday against Minnesota when he suffered an undisclosed, lower-body injury at the end of the first half. He had carried 12 times for 126 yards and a touchdown before exiting and not returning for the rest of the Lions' 42-14 victory . Over the past three games, the resurgent tailback from Lakeville, Minnesota has run for 341 yards (7.9 yards per carry) and three touchdowns. He had averaged just 4 yards per carry and gained little traction in an inconsistent start to the season. At least Penn State does have a productive fallback option now. Sophomore backup Cam Wallace has carried 44 times for 273 yards (6.2 average) in the past three games, including a career-best 135 yards against Purdue. "I know if anybody can do it, (Hansen will) be ready to play," Campbell said. "But if it's not Carson, obviously Cam has stepped into a major role, has proven that he's ready to go when opportunities come his way. "I (also) thought James Peoples really did a great job in the second half (against Minnesota) ... And then, equally, I said this a lot about Quentin (Martin) ... that he's got the ability to do it. So, I feel really good about the depth in that room and guys that we trust (to) carry the football." Wallace did stand out in Hansen's absence against Minnesota. He ran for 82 yards on 15 carries and caught a 1-yard touchdown pass. Frank Bodani covers Penn State football for the York Daily Record and USA Today Network. Contact him at fbodani@ydr.com and follow him on X, formerly known as Twitter, @YDRPennState. item.title: Three Hurricanes Prospects Detroit Should Want for Larkin
item.description: Detroit Red Wings center Dylan Larkin has told Detroit he would accept a trade to the Carolina Hurricanes , one of the 10 teams he has signed off on , which is what makes a Larkin trade with Carolina more than a hypothetical. Larkin played 10 games for Detroit this season before the Red Wings suspended him without pay on Oct. 29, after he informed the team he would no longer play for them. He scored two goals and recorded four assists in those 10 games, along with a plus/minus rating of 3. Interim general manager Shawn Horcoff said the goal in any Larkin deal is “to get players who can help us right away.” A young center and some draft picks are the kind of return that would fit. If the Red Wings make a deal with Carolina, what are some prospects that they should want back? Oct 24, 2026; Calgary, Alberta, CAN; Detroit Red Wings center Dylan Larkin (71) skates with the puck against the Calgary Flames during the second period at Scotiabank Saddledome. Mandatory Credit: Sergei Belski-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Bradly Nadeau Is Carolina’s Top-Ranked Prospect Bradly Nadeau is a left winger in the Hurricanes organization , and Daily Faceoff ranked him first in Carolina’s system in its July breakdown of the pool. Nadeau is 21 years old and was the 30th overall pick, a first-round selection, in the 2023 NHL Draft. He has played in three games this season for Carolina, where he recorded two assists and a plus/minus rating of -1. In 13 AHL games with the Chicago Wolves, Carolina’s affiliate, he scored five goals and recorded six assists, along with a plus/minus rating of -5. Felix Unger-Sorum Is Already Getting NHL Minutes Right winger Felix Unger-Sorum is also 21 years old and was a second-round selection, 62nd overall, in the 2023 NHL Draft. The same Daily Faceoff breakdown ranked him second , right behind Nadeau. Unger-Sorum has played three games for Carolina this season without a point, and he has one assist in four career NHL games. In 12 AHL games with Chicago, he has scored two goals and has recorded six assists, along with a plus/minus rating of -6. Unger-Sorum would be an interesting trade candidate for the Red Wings because he is already getting some NHL minutes with Carolina. Charlie Cerrato Would Add Center Depth in a Larkin Trade Charlie Cerrato is a centerman. He was the 49th overall pick, a second-round selection, in the 2025 NHL Draft by Carolina, and Daily Faceoff slotted him seventh in the same pool. Cerrato is currently playing for the Wolves in the AHL. In seven AHL games with Chicago this season, he has scored one goal and has recorded three assists, along with a plus/minus rating of 1. Cerrato is also 21 years old. These are three of the prospects Detroit should ask Carolina about in a trade for Larkin. Obviously, the Red Wings won’t get all three of them, but they need to come away with at least one of them if a deal happens.

item.title: Stephen Curry assumed last summer's contract extension might be last one
item.description: Nov 11, 2026; Houston, Texas, USA; Golden State Warriors guard Stephen Curry (30) holds his side during the first quarter against the Houston Rockets at Toyota Center. Mandatory Credit: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect How much the Golden State Warriors still rely on Stephen Curry has been painfully obvious since he went down with an oblique abdominal tear: 0-3, with the losses by a combined 66 points, and the Warriors failed to score 100 points in the last two. Even before this injury, last season's knee issues had Curry being realistic about his future when speaking with Anthony Slater of ESPN for a must-read story. Curry signed a two-year, $115.9 million extension last summer that could take him for two seasons beyond this one (the second of those years is a player option). "I assumed that it would probably be one of, if not the last, contract I signed. I'm not afraid to say it. But maybe I'll surprise myself and want to keep going." Curry has accepted where he is in his career. He still wants to win (which is why he didn't take a max extension) and says he would take on a smaller role if that's what helps the team. Curry also discusses how he had to alter his intense off-season workout routine to give his body more time to recover — he can't just push through everything anymore. None of that has shown on the court this season, as Curry has been spectacular, averaging 27.8 points per game while shooting 45.7% from 3-point range. He's doing that in reduced minutes — coach Steve Kerr is trying to keep him at around 28 minutes a night — and with less movement, to ease things on those older knees. None of that diminishes Curry's incredible gravity, which draws defenders and opens things up for rookie sensation Yaxel Landeborg to get off to a fast start. With Curry out the past couple of games and defenses focused on him, things have been tougher for Landeborg. Things will get easier for Curry and the Warriors when Jimmy Butler (torn ACL) and Moses Moody (ruptured patellar tendon) return from injuries, expected later this season. Until then, the Warriors have to find a way to stay in the postseason mix in a deep West. Curry, for his part, is still in this to win it, but he may be taking more time to stop and smell the roses, he told ESPN. "I want to appreciate what's happening right now because I don't want to just go through the motions," Curry said. "Then, it passes you by."

item.title: Key midfielder absent as Real Madrid return to training ahead of Celta Vigo clash
item.description: Key midfielder absent as Real Madrid return to training ahead of Celta Vigo clash Real Madrid returned to training today after Jose Mourinho gave his players a few days off during the current international break. The squad began preparations for Saturday’s La Liga meeting with Celta Vigo at the Santiago Bernabeu, but question marks remain over the availability of key midfielder Aurelien Tchouameni. Tchouameni trains indoors Indeed, as confirmed by the club’s official website , Tchouameni was not part of the group training session today and worked indoors separately from the rest of the squad. The French midfielder picked up a groin injury while training with his national team ahead of their first match during the international break last week. Absent from training. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Tchouameni returned to Madrid immediately and while a serious issue was ruled out, his availability for the weekend game against Celta Vigo has been cast into doubt . Real Madrid will keep monitoring the 26-year-old midfielder’s progress over the coming days and the coaching staff will assess his condition on a day-to-day basis before deciding whether he can be included in the squad. As things stand, Tchouameni’s participation against the Galician outfit is far from guaranteed, and Los Blancos are unlikely to take unnecessary risks with a player who is integral into Mourinho’s plans. So far this season, Tchouameni has played ten games in all competitions for Real Madrid, managing one assist in the process. A doubt to face Celta Vigo. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) The 26-year-old has already missed four games this season due to a muscle injury he sustained during the World Cup. As such, the Merengues will be careful not to rush things with his recovery from the latest setback. Rodrygo, Asencio continue recovery Meanwhile, the training update from the club stated that today’s session overseen by Mourinho included physical work, pressing and ball-recovery exercises, followed by small-sided matches on smaller pitches. A number of players from the youth teams were also involved in the session. Apart from Tchouameni and the players away on international duty, Raul Asencio and Rodrygo were also absent from the training session today. The Real Madrid pair continued their respective recovery programmes as they work towards returning to full fitness.

item.title: DME Academy basketball 4-star prospect K'Majay Jenkins signs with Kansas
item.description: K'Majay Jenkins is headed to one of college basketball’s bluebloods, and he’ll arrive early. The DME Academy basketball standout reclassified from 2028 to 2027 and signed with Kansas on Nov. 17. He received an offer from the Jayhawks and visited campus late last month. “We're excited about K'Majay,” Kansas head coach Bill Self said in a news release . “We think he is one of the most athletic and one of the highest ceiling players in this year's high school class. “We feel K'Majay's athleticism and motor should put him in position for a smooth transition to Division I basketball at both ends of the floor. He has shown that he can play above the rim and can rebound at an elite level.” 247Sports ranked Jenkins as the 52nd-best prospect in the Class of 2028 before he reclassified. He holds a four-star rating. The 6-foot-6 small forward backed that up by averaging 27 points, 10 rebounds and six assists on the AAU circuit over the summer. He put up 13.1 points and seven rebounds for DME last winter. Jenkins, who hails from Anderson, South Carolina, chose Kansas over the likes of Cal, Clemson, Florida State and South Carolina. item.title: What can we expect from Tiger Woods at the Hero? A review of his returns after long layoffs
item.description: As unfortunate as it is, Tiger Woods is no stranger to returning to competition after a long time away due to injuries and other personal struggles. Woods will tee it up next month at the 2026 Hero World Challenge, an event he hosts in the Bahamas. This will mark his first competitive start since the 2024 British Open , where he missed the cut. The time since has been filled with more surgeries, another car crash , an arrest and rehab stint and plenty more. He announced Tuesday that he will return to competitive golf at the Hero, where he will walk 72 holes at a no-cut event. It's the first time he has done that since the 2024 Masters. So what should we expect from Big Cat? Here's a breakdown of how he has fared in his return to competition after lengthy layoffs throughout his career. 2009 WGC-Accenture Match Play — T-17 Woods' return from an eight-month layoff ended abruptly as South African Tim Clark bested the top golfer in the world 4 and 2 in the second round of the event. It was Woods' first tournament since his gritty U.S. Open victory at Torrey Pines, which was followed by knee surgery. 2010 Masters — T-4 Tiger missed five months before teeing it up at the 2010 Masters, but it hardly hindered his performance, as he finished in a tie for fourth, five shots behind winner Phil Mickelson, who won by three. 2016 Hero World Challenge — 15th In late 2015, Woods has three surgeries on his back, which kept him out of competition for more than a year. He finished 15th at his event in the Bahamas, one of only two events he played in the 2016-17 season. 2017 Hero World Challenge — T-9 Another year, another return in the Bahamas after a long layoff ― this one coming after a fourth back surgery, a spinal fusion. It started the trek to him winning the 2019 Masters. 2022 Masters — 47th A severe car wreck in early 2021 resulted in Woods missing more than a year of competition and having his right leg severely injured. The surgery essentially rebuilt his leg. However, he made the cut in his return, but there were some clear signs of discomfort walking the severe slopes of Augusta National. 2023 Genesis — T-45 In his first start since missing the cut at the 150th Open Championship, Woods made the cut at Riviera and proceeded to finish T-45. 2023 Hero World Challenge — 18th Tiger returned after ankle surgery in 2023 and finished 18th in the Bahamas. item.title: Ben Earl backs surprise location to host 2028 Nations Championship finals weekend
item.description: The England rugby No 8 Ben Earl believes the next finals weekend of rugby’s Nations Championship should be held away from a traditional stronghold of the sport, floating Las Vegas and Brazil as possible candidates for the showpiece event. Twickenham’s Allianz Stadium will host the inaugural finals next weekend, with six games held across three days based on pool placings across the July and November international windows. England are vying with France and Ireland to top the northern hemisphere pool, while New Zealand and South Africa are assured of top-two finishes in the southern hemisphere group. Earl had been a critic of the new competition during England’s demanding itinerary earlier in the year, with Steve Borthwick ’s side playing Tests in Johannesburg, Liverpool and Santiago del Estero across consecutive Saturdays in July. But the 28-year-old has come around on the format, and believes it offers a good opportunity to grow the game. “I feel like it's taking shape nicely now,” Earl said. “I don't want to say I was wrong because that's not my style. But you can see the method in it now. The summer obviously needs a tweak in whatever way that looks like. “There's some big games this weekend. Hopefully for the fans, they've enjoyed it. We certainly enjoyed playing in it. And obviously, it's a bit nicer being at home.” France and Spain are understood to have registered interest in hosting the finals weekend in the future, while Rugby Football Union (RFU) chief executive Bill Sweeney also indicated that Twickenham would be willing to hold the event again. It had been mooted that Qatar would be the venue for the 2028 edition, though that is thought to be off the table after a sponsorship deal with Qatar Airways fell through amid the conflict in the Middle East. Ben Earl has come around on the Nations Championship (Reuters) A number of top Tests will be held in the United States, though, over the next half-decade as World Rugby builds up to the 2031 Rugby World Cup, and Earl believes “Sin City” would be an ideal fit. “You'd be hard pressed not to say Vegas, wouldn't you? That would be a good fun,” Earl admitted. “People in Brazil apparently love the game. What about something cool like that? Like, I don't know, take it somewhere where there's tier two nations. And we all get a chance to go somewhere new that we haven't been before, because we're all in the entertainment industry at the end of the day. Let's try and grow the game. “We know if we go to London, we know if we go to wherever, people are going to turn up and watch because people love it. But let's go somewhere cool, like a Hong Kong or a Spain. “There's obvious places that we didn't get a chance to go to that would be cool.” England face New Zealand in their final pool fixture on Saturday afternoon.

item.title: Antonelli joins exclusive F1 club with achievement unseen for 44 years
item.description: Kimi Antonelli 's remarkable 2026 campaign has earned him a place in an exclusive group of world champions, becoming just the sixth driver in history to claim his maiden Grand Prix victory and first world title in the same season. The Mercedes youngster has already rewritten several records during his second year in Formula 1 , most notably becoming the youngest world champion in the sport's history at the age of 20. His championship triumph in Mexico City also ended a 73-year wait for an Italian drivers' champion, with Alberto Ascari previously securing the title in 1953. However, another extraordinary statistic highlights just how unusual Antonelli's achievement has been. Despite Formula 1 having crowned world champions since 1950, only five drivers before the Italian had managed to secure their first race victory and maiden championship within the same calendar year. Antonelli ends 44-year wait for rare F1 achievement Antonelli's first Formula 1 victory came at the Chinese Grand Prix in March, when he converted his maiden pole position into a win for Mercedes. It was an important breakthrough for the Italian, who had completed his rookie campaign in 2025 without reaching the top step of the podium. What initially represented a major career milestone eventually became the starting point of a championship-winning season. Antonelli continued to establish himself as a title contender, adding further victories before securing the championship with a third-place finish at the Mexican Grand Prix in November. Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures The last driver to accomplish the same feat was Keke Rosberg in 1982. The Finnish driver secured his maiden victory at the Swiss Grand Prix, held at Dijon-Prenois in France, before going on to win his only world championship later that year. Interestingly, Rosberg achieved the feat with just one victory throughout the entire campaign, underlining how different his championship-winning season was from Antonelli's dominant 2026 performance. Before Rosberg, the achievement had last been recorded by Denny Hulme in 1967, when the New Zealander claimed his first victory in Monaco before winning the championship with Brabham. The list also features Graham Hill, who secured both milestones in 1962, and Jack Brabham, who did so in 1959. Giuseppe Farina was the first driver to accomplish the feat, winning the inaugural Formula 1 title race at Silverstone in 1950 before becoming the sport's first world champion. Antonelli's inclusion means that two Italian drivers now feature among the six names, with Farina and the Mercedes youngster separated by 76 years. item.title: Wayne Rooney reveals “lowest point” of Man United career he was “contemplating suicide”
item.description: Wayne Rooney reveals “lowest point” of Man United career he was “contemplating suicide” Manchester United icon Wayne Rooney has revealed that he considered taking his own life during the height of his career at the club. Legend Widely considered one of, if not United’s greatest players ever, Rooney arrived at the club from Everton in 2004 as an 18-year-old for a then-British record fee for a teenager. He announced himself with an explosive Champions League debut, netting a sensational hat-trick against Fenerbahçe. He then rapidly became a key player under Sir Alex Ferguson, taking the PFA Young Player of the Year in his first season before adding the PFA Fans’ Player of the Year the following year. Primarily leading the line, Rooney was a key figure in Sir Alex’s various United sides and in the club’s dominance during the 2000s. The Englishman helped United win five Premier League titles, the UEFA Champions League, the FIFA Club World Cup, an FA Cup, four League Cups and the Europa League. Across all competitions, Rooney made 559 appearances and contributed 253 goals. He still retains the crown of being United’s record goalscorer, having overtaken the legendary Sir Bobby Charlton in 2017. Rooney left United in 2017 at age 31 to seal a return to Everton. He spoke on the Life at the Midpoint with Gabby Logan podcast and revealed that despite the incredible success he enjoyed on the pitch, he struggled off it and even contemplated suicide. Rooney’s admission Rooney said, “I can look back and say I was selfish, but I knew I was going through something which I was really struggling to deal with. Then I didn’t want Kai seeing me like that, so that’s why I’d hide away as well.” “I got to a place where you’re contemplating suicide. You just didn’t want to be around anyone. I didn’t want to be see people in the streets. I didn’t want to go into shops. I was always comfortable on a football pitch, but everything else [I] really struggled with it.” He added, “You don’t want to show any weakness, so you try to mask it. Even though I knew the position I was in, it was difficult to actually admit that I was in that in that position because I felt like you feel less of a man if you like for doing that.” “I was speaking to a therapist to try and figure out what was up with me because when I look back I was probably at the height of my career, I’ve just had a young son, I’ve just been married. It should be the happiest point in my life and it wasn’t.” “It was probably the lowest point because of the selfish acts I was taking.”
